Readings held in `READINGS` (`src/tide_cache.py:1`) no longer stay for ever: a reading older than 14 days expires instead of accumulating through `store` (`src/tide_cache.py:4`, `src/tide_cache.py:5`). - **Retention period:** 14 days, held in one module constant. This is an operator-stated constraint. Question asked: how many days should a tide reading be kept before it expires? Answer given: keep readings for 14 days. The repository and vault state no period of their own. - **Stored time:** `store` appends the reading as given and records no time (`src/tide_cache.py:5`), so each entry in `READINGS` becomes a `(stored_at, reading)` pair, with `stored_at` read from `time.time()`. `store` keeps its one-argument signature (`src/tide_cache.py:4`). Nothing else in the repository reads `READINGS` or calls `store`, so no caller needs changing. - **When expiry runs:** at the end of each `store` call, which is the module's only function (`src/tide_cache.py:4`). It removes, in place, every entry whose age at that call is more than 14 days. A stale reading therefore leaves at the next `store`, and no background job or read function is added.
